problem: End-to-end DRL/IL visual navigation policies need huge amounts of experience because they learn purely from pixels without intermediate scene representations. Existing scene graph generation methods need heavy manual graph annotation, output semantically meaningless relations, or are too costly to run inside a policy.
motivation: Humans build compact object-level 3D topology representations to navigate efficiently. A sparse scene-graph encoder that captures objects and their geometric relations could improve sample efficiency and give interpretable intermediate representations. Simulator rendering data already contains the needed geometry, so no manual annotation is needed.
key_idea: Use a Graph Transformer Network as the visual encoder of the navigation policy, trained end-to-end with policy gradients plus renderer-supervised node and edge labels, so it emits a sparse 3D scene graph while refining visual features.
insight: Structurally refined object features make the policy more sample-efficient: with equal 14M-step training, GraphMapper nearly doubles SPL over a same-backbone ResNet50 RGB-D baseline (the ResNet50 baseline underperforms even the Blind agent). Combining GraphMapper with depth or a projected top-down map gives the best results in both PointGoal and VLN, so the graph features complement geometric maps. In VLN, GraphMapper alone (SR 0.18) is below Depth (0.24) but far above RGB (0.03), showing that implicit 3D positions carry useful information.
method: Renderer-supervised ground truth: node labels (Matterport object classes) and edge types (co-planarity in x/y/z and same-region) are computed automatically from the simulator's semantic 3D mesh and bounding boxes, so no manual annotation is needed.

Graph-based observations: simulator semantic masks serve as ROIs (a detector could replace them); ResNet50 features form node inputs; a complete graph with N(N-1) candidate edges uses 6-D edge features (object dimensions plus front-plane location from depth).
Graph Transformer layers: 3 GT layers softly select and compose edge types into multi-hop meta-path adjacency matrices (C channels, identity included).

GCN and heads: a 3-layer GCN per channel produces concatenated node features; a node-class head (cross-entropy) and a multi-label edge-type head (BCE on the adjacency tensor); gradients from the policy loss also flow into the encoder.

Policy integration: for PointGoal, the ResNet18 in the RL+Res18 baseline is replaced by GraphMapper (node features pooled, GRU actor-critic, PPO, with an auxiliary scene-graph coverage reward); for VLN, the Seq2Seq baseline uses teacher-forcing IL. A ProjDepth or Depth variant adds a depth or top-down map branch.
Downstream uses: accumulating graphs over a trajectory gives unsupervised room separation via 'same room' edges, and attention scores give action interpretability.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 (ImageNet + MSCOCO pretrained) + Graph Transformer Network + GCN, with GRU policy (trained with PPO or teacher forcing)
setting.training_data: PointGoal: Matterport3D train split, 14M steps of RL; VLN: VLN-CE train split, at most 30 epochs of teacher-forcing IL; scene graph supervision auto-extracted from the simulator
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus ROI/semantic masks from the simulator (GT semantic masks used as ROIs), PointGoal GPS/compass target for PointGoal
setting.action_space: low-level: turn left/right, move forward, stop (VLN-CE: forward 0.25 m, turn 15°)
setting.privileged: GT semantic masks/ROIs from the simulator rendering engine at test time; GT scene graph used for training supervision and for the coverage reward

numbers.backbone: ResNet50 + Graph Transformer Network + Depth encoder, Seq2Seq
numbers.extra: GT semantic-mask ROIs; teacher-forcing IL only; val-seen split
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Several VLN agents on VLN-CE validation-seen set (values printed as fractions; SR 0.27)

numbers.backbone: ResNet50 + Graph Transformer Network, Seq2Seq (no depth branch)
numbers.extra: GT semantic-mask ROIs; depth used only implicitly for 3D positions

numbers_note: PointGoal results are given only in a bar-chart figure (Fig. quant), so no numbers are extracted. VLN-CE metrics are printed as fractions (0.27), not percentages; kept exactly as printed. The val-unseen table is commented out in the source.
results: On VLN-CE val-seen, GraphMapper-Depth reaches SR 0.27 / SPL 0.26 versus the RGB-Depth baseline at 0.25 / 0.24, and GraphMapper alone (SR 0.18) is far above RGB (0.03). On Habitat PointGoal (Matterport3D val, 495 episodes, 14M steps), GraphMapper+ProjDepth performs best, and GraphMapper nearly doubles SPL over the ResNet50 RGB-D baseline.
limitations: Uses simulator ground-truth semantic masks as ROIs, and evaluation is only in Habitat on Matterport3D with no real-robot tests; a real detector is not evaluated.

VLN gains over the RGB-Depth baseline are small (SR 0.27 vs 0.25) and only val-seen is reported; GraphMapper alone loses to Depth-only. In PointGoal, SPL decreases relative to a standalone ResNet50 baseline, which the authors attribute to the coverage reward.
